tasks.title: Real facts
tasks.statement: During the night between 29th and 30th of October 2013, two astronomers Ovidiu Tercu and Alex Dumitriu from the Astronomic Observatory from Galati, Romania discovered an asteroid in the Torro constellation. The asteroid named 2013 UX11 has a diameter of D = 2,5 km. This was the first time that an asteroid was discovered by Romanian astronomer in order to make this problem for IOAA. After analyzing the data in the “Minor Planet Center” the following communication was received: 2013 UX11 is an asteroid from the Main Belt of Asteroids, orbiting between the orbits of Mars an Jupiter with period T = 4,2 years with an eccentricity e = 0,15.

parts.question: a) Find out the characteristics of orbit of the 2013 UX11 regardless to the Sun- (a, b, c, rmin, rmax). You know the mass of the Sun M = 9,1 * 10^30 kg and the gravitational constant K = 6,67 * 10^-11 Nm^2 kg^-2.
parts.reference: a) Formulas and calculations for semi-major axis a, semi-minor axis b, distance from center to focus c, rmin and rmax. Results: a approx 3 * 10^8 km; b approx 2.96 * 10^8 km; c approx 0.488 * 10^8 km; rmin approx 2.512 * 10^8 km; rmax approx 3.488 * 10^8 km.

parts.question: b) Find out the maximum and respectively the minimum of the temperatures of the surface of the asteroid. You know: Temperature of the surface of the Sun TS = 6000 K; the radius of the Sun RS approx 7 * 10^5 km; the albedo of the surface of the asteroid alpha = 0,2.
parts.reference: b) Energy balance equation considering solar radiation and asteroid emission. TA,max approx 211.64 K (at perihelium); TA,min approx 179.60 K (at aphelium).

tasks.title: The plan - A. For a given speed of the missile
tasks.statement: You have received a scaled sketch of the positions of the Earth (P), satellite (S) and the point where the missile have to hit the asteroid. The distance between asteroid and the Earth is r = 30000 km. You have to analyze the problem of saving the Earth only by using the materials from the box in the conditions that for a given speed of the missile v0, the problem has only one solution i.e. there is only one trajectory from S to A, available for the missile in order to hit the asteroid.

parts.question: a) the elements of the missile trajectory;
parts.reference: a) Measurements from the sketch and calculations: r0, r, d, delta r, x, y, 2a, a, 2b, b, 2c, c, e, rmin, rmax, and real scale scaled values.

parts.question: b) the direction of the initial speed of the missile v0 in order to be able to hit the asteroid. Indicate on the paper sheet the angle you measured.
c) Calculate the launch velocity of the missile v0 if you know the mass of the Earth M = 6 * 10^24 kg and the gravitational constant K = 6,67 * 10^-11 Nm^2 kg^-2
parts.reference: c) Calculation of v0 using vis-viva equation or orbital energy relations. v0 approx 3.2 km/s.

parts.question: d) Using the plasticine imagine a very simple device in order to calculate the duration of missile flight from launch until the impact with the asteroid.
parts.reference: d) Kepler's third law applied to the trajectory ellipse. Total period T approx 7.56 h, flight duration calculated via geometric proportions using plasticine/ruler setup approx 3.19 h.

parts.question: e) Using the wire, measure the distance covered by the missile from the launch-point to the impact-point.
parts.reference: e) Wire measurement along ellipse arc: lSA approx 135 mm, real distance lSA,real approx 26470.58 km.

tasks.title: The plan - B. Two solutions
tasks.statement: To be sure that the asteroid will be destroyed from another satellite orbiting the Earth at another altitude will be launched in the same moment of time, a second missile in order to hit the asteroid simultaneously with the first missile. Notations P – center of the Earth; S – launch position of the new missile, A – the impact point at distance r = 30000 km from the Earth. In this configuration you know that there are two possible trajectories, from S to A for the second missile. For that a mysterious point X is marked on the sketch.

parts.question: a) the elements of the two possible trajectories.
parts.reference: a) Two ellipses with a common focus, determination of semi-axes a, b1, b2, c1, c2 for both trajectories.

parts.question: b) For each trajectory determine the directions of the launch-speeds, at the same velocity which allows the missile to hit the target;
parts.reference: b) Launch angles: alpha' approx 50 degrees; alpha" approx 70 degrees.

parts.question: c) The launch- velocity v0, if you know the mass of the Earth M = 6 * 10^24 kg and the gravitational constant G = 6.67 * 10^-11 Nm^2 kg^-2;
parts.reference: c) Calculation of v0 for case B, v0 approx 3.6 km/s.

parts.question: d) Using the plasticine imagine a very simple device in order to calculate the durations of missile flight from launch till the impact with the asteroid for the both trajectories
parts.reference: d) Total period T approx 10 h, flight durations for both ellipses calculated via proportional devices: approx 5.64 h and approx 3.975 h.

parts.question: e) Using the wire, measure the distances covered by the missile from launch-point to the impact-point.
parts.reference: e) Wire measurements for both trajectories: lSA' approx 51308.41 km; lSA" approx 43738.31 km.

tasks.title: C. Security zone
tasks.statement: You have to delimitate around the Earth a security zone. From the point A of this problem you know that there is a unique possible trajectory for the defensive missile. This means that the point A on the sketch is locate on a curve which delimitates a security zone for the Earth.

parts.question: a) If you know that the triangle defined by the points P- the Earth, S – Sun, A – impact point remains unchanged in time establish the shape of the curve which delimitates the security zone
parts.reference: a) Establishing the shape of the security zone curve (ellipse equation derivation).

parts.question: b) Draw on the paper this curve and determine its parameters
parts.reference: b) Parameters of the security ellipse: 2a0,real approx 52352.94 km, c0,real approx 13039 km, b0,real approx 22697.84 km, e0 approx 0.5.

parts.question: c) Where have to be situated the impact – point A in order to hit the asteroid simultaneously with to missiles
parts.reference: c) Geometric positioning requirements for simultaneous impact based on the security zone properties.

parts.question: d) Use your plasticine device to find out the time spent by an fragment of the asteroid which flies after the impact with the missile, on the curve which delimitates the security zone
parts.reference: d) Total period T0 approx 11.67 h, flight time calculation for the fragment on the security curve approx 7.36 h.
